changes.before: Add controls and an English caption track to the video, controls to the audio, and a visible transcript link outside both players.
changes.after: Give media playback controls, captions and a readable transcript.

before: video and audio embed media. The controls attribute asks the browser to show playback controls.

A source element names a media file and can state its type.
```html
<audio controls>
  <source src="birds.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
</audio>
```
The file must exist and be supported; markup alone does not supply a recording.

A track element can attach timed captions to video. Captions include meaningful sounds as well as speech. Here is the track in a complete structural example. ```html

Read the pond study transcript

```
WebVTT is a text format for timed cues. Matching src, language and label is not proof that captions are accurate or synchronized.
A transcript gives another way to read the information. Keep its link outside the media element so it remains available even when the browser supports the player but cannot load the recording.
Fallback text inside audio or video is for browsers that do not support that element; it is not a reliable error message for every media-loading failure.
For this practice, file names are example references. The checks inspect structure; they do not download, play, transcribe or verify media.
after: `<video>` adds a video player, and `<audio>` adds an audio player. Add `controls` so people can start, pause and adjust playback. Let the person start the media instead of using autoplay.

A `<source>` points to a recording.

```html
<audio controls>
  <source src="birds.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
</audio>
```

`src` names the file. `type` says which file format it uses. The recording must exist and work in the browser; these tags do not create it.

A `` can give a video timed captions: words for speech and important sounds. ```html

Read the pond study transcript

``` `kind="captions"` says what the track is for. `src` names its file. `srclang="en"` marks English, and `label="English"` names the choice in the player.
A WebVTT file stores caption text with the times when it should appear. Its filename usually ends in `.vtt`. The captions need to match both the recording’s words and their timing.
A transcript is a readable copy of the recording’s information. Put its link outside the player so readers can find it even when the media will not play.

Text placed inside audio or video can appear in browsers that do not support that player. It may stay hidden when a supported player fails to load its file. That is why the separate transcript link matters.

Add controls to both starter players. Inside video, add English captions from `exploration-en.vtt`. After both players, add a link to `exploration-transcript.html` with `transcript` in its visible text. The files are practice names, not included recordings. Run the markup checks; they do not test playback.

before.question: The browser supports video but the file fails to load. Where should the transcript link be so it remains available?
choices: Only inside video as fallback text
Outside the video element in ordinary page content
before.explanation: Supported media elements do not guarantee their fallback children appear on a load failure. A separate visible link remains available independently of playback.

after.question: A browser supports video, but the recording fails to load. Where should its transcript link be?
choices: Outside the video in ordinary page content.
after.explanation: A link outside the player remains available even when the recording cannot play.

before: controls is a Boolean attribute: add it to each player.
Put track inside video and keep the transcript link outside both players.
after: Use kind="captions", src="exploration-en.vtt", srclang="en" and label="English".
The transcript link goes after the closing video and audio tags.
No media download or playback is needed for these checks.

changes.before: Media and caption paths are placeholders, not supplied assets. Automated checks certify markup only. Before publishing, supply real media, a transcript and accurate synchronized WebVTT captions; test playback, captions and keyboard controls in a browser.
